structure: Part 1, the whole ruling file: all 37 lines of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-19.md, read in full, nothing held back for another part. The file has three pieces in order, and this part covers every one of them. First a three-line preamble (lines 3 to 5) naming the session the ruling was given in (the overview-and-review build session) and the engineering review it answers (review:engineering-2026-11-19, a separate source), which had listed what the theme does differently from the service's existing patterns. Then Sam's own ruling as five numbered items (lines 7 to 20): item 1 the plants notification task list heading and its copy; item 2 one form per header button; item 3 how tests find live animals review cards, the review page object's single heading and the removal of two shared helpers' overloads; item 4 that every other atypical item the review found is fixed, with a four-bullet sub-list of the exceptions that stay as they are (the local stack's uploader restart, the deleted plants journey spec ruling, the tests repo's deleted docs note on Cancel amend, and the animals backend unit tests that build a real DocumentService on stubbed repositories); item 5 as few increments as sensible. Then a closing block (lines 22 to 37) headed "Orchestrator's calls applying it, which Sam accepted (\"crack on\")", holding all eight applied calls: the animals backend dropping the stored outstanding items list and the rule on the OutstandingItem enum (which explicitly replaces the 16 November ruling's "what stays" clause, claim 2, and keeps the submitted date), the non-null yes/no "Answers differ from submitted" flag, the animals frontend stub taking "answers changed" from the backend's shape, a real GOV.UK heading class for "Identification details", review cards' accessible names, the standard page not found for a missing notification on the review page, the missing blank line in the plants notification lifecycle spec, and Delete staying a link to the delete confirmation page outside the Amend and Copy as new forms. The claims keep the two blocks' different authority on their face: items 1 to 5 are Sam's own wording, the eight bullets are the orchestrator's calls that Sam accepted. Claims are recorded in file order, with the gaps the ruling leaves on points it touches recorded last.

claims.statement: The ruling was given in the overview-and-review build session and answers the theme's engineering review review:engineering-2026-11-19, which had listed what the theme does differently from the service's existing patterns, so the ruling's subject matter is that review's list of differences.
claims.quote: Given in the overview-and-review build session, answering the theme's engineering review (review:engineering-2026-11-19, https://claude.ai/artifact/TrAdrBupdoyCP4YJmXjuJL), which listed what the theme does differently from the service's existing patterns.
claims.note: Context for every other claim in this part. The engineering review itself is a separate source, not part of this one.

claims.statement: The plants frontend shows the notification task list heading visibly, as the live animals frontend already does.
claims.quote: **Plants shows the notification task list heading visibly**, as live animals does.

claims.statement: The notification task list heading reads "Notification task list".
claims.quote: The copy is **"Notification task list"**

claims.statement: "task list" in that heading is spelled as two words, which the ruling names as the GOV.UK spelling.
claims.quote: ("task list" as two words, the GOV.UK spelling)

claims.statement: The "Notification task list" copy applies in both services, live animals and plants.
claims.quote: The copy is **"Notification task list"** ("task list" as two words, the GOV.UK spelling) in both services.
claims.note: "both services" is read as live animals and plants, the two the item names.

claims.statement: Each button on the notification view header gets its own form, as every other posting button in the service does.
claims.quote: **Each header button gets its own form**, as every other posting button in the service does

claims.statement: The header actions the one-form-each rule covers are Amend, Copy as new and Delete on the notification view header.
claims.quote: Amend, Copy as new and Delete on the notification view header
claims.note: Applied call 8 (claim ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-032 and ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-033) settles how Delete meets this rule: it stays a link outside both forms.

claims.statement: The one-form-each header rule applies in both the live animals frontend and the plants frontend.
claims.quote: in both the live animals and plants frontends

claims.statement: Tests find live animals review cards by GOV.UK structure and role, the way the plants tests already do.
claims.quote: **Tests find live animals review cards the way plants does**, by GOV.UK structure and role

claims.statement: No test depends on the words "2. Description of the goods".
claims.quote: so no test depends on the words "2. Description of the goods"

claims.statement: The review page's test page object gets a single `heading` again.
claims.quote: The review page's test page object gets a single `heading` again
claims.note: "again" says the single heading existed before the theme's change and is being restored.

claims.statement: The overloads that grew on the two shared test helpers, resume in the UI and the save and continue walk, are removed.
claims.quote: the overloads that grew on the two shared helpers (resume in the UI, the save and continue walk) come out

claims.statement: Every other atypical item the engineering review found is fixed, apart from the four exceptions the ruling names.
claims.quote: **Every other atypical item the review found is fixed**, except these, which stay as they are:
claims.note: Which items that covers is in the engineering review, a separate source; see the gap claim ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-036.

claims.statement: The local stack's automatic restart of the file uploader stays as it is and is kept.
claims.quote: the local stack's automatic restart of the file uploader (keep);

claims.statement: The plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded stays as it is; the ruling records no interest in changing it.
claims.quote: the plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded (don't care);

claims.statement: The tests repo's deleted docs note on why Cancel amend waits on the URL stays as it is; the ruling records no interest in restoring it.
claims.quote: the tests repo's deleted docs note on why Cancel amend waits on the URL (don't care);

claims.statement: The animals backend unit tests that build a real DocumentService on stubbed repositories stay as they are and are kept, because they follow the house rule of not mocking the service's own modules.
claims.quote: the animals backend unit tests that build a real DocumentService on stubbed repositories (keep: they follow the house rule of not mocking the service's own modules).

claims.statement: The fixes land in as few increments as sensible, not one increment per item.
claims.quote: **As few increments as sensible**, not one per item.

claims.statement: The eight bullets that close the file are the orchestrator's calls applying the ruling, which Sam accepted with "crack on", so each is decided rather than proposed.
claims.quote: Orchestrator's calls applying it, which Sam accepted ("crack on"):
claims.note: Authority marker for claims ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-020 to ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-034: they carry the owner's acceptance of the orchestrator's wording, a lesser authority on their face than items 1 to 5, which are Sam's own words.

claims.statement: The animals backend stops storing the outstanding items list, the health-certificate-owed list that nothing reads.
claims.quote: The animals backend stops storing the outstanding items list (the health-certificate-owed list nothing reads)

claims.statement: The rule that works out the outstanding items comes off the OutstandingItem enum.
claims.quote: and the rule that works it out comes off the OutstandingItem enum

claims.statement: Both the stored outstanding items list and the rule that works it out are re-added later, with the future outstanding-actions banner.
claims.quote: Both are re-added with the future outstanding-actions banner.

claims.statement: This call replaces the 16 November ruling's "what stays: submitting records ... the outstanding items" (its claim 2), so that earlier ruling no longer keeps the outstanding items.
claims.quote: This replaces the 16 November ruling's "what stays: submitting records ... the outstanding items" (claim 2)
claims.note: An explicit supersession of ruling:sam-2026-11-16 claim 2 on the outstanding items only; the reconciler should treat this ruling as the later word on that point.

claims.statement: The submitted date is still recorded by the animals backend.
claims.quote: the submitted date is still recorded
claims.note: Carves the submitted date out of the supersession in claim ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-023: of the 16 November ruling's "what stays" list, only the outstanding items go.

claims.statement: "Answers differ from submitted" is a non-null yes/no flag.
claims.quote: "Answers differ from submitted" is a non-null yes/no flag.

claims.statement: The animals frontend's local stub takes "answers changed" from the backend's shape, as a stored flag kept the way the backend keeps it, rather than working the value out itself.
claims.quote: The animals frontend's local stub takes "answers changed" from the backend's shape (a stored flag, kept as the backend keeps it) rather than working it out itself.
claims.note: "answers changed" here is the same flag applied call 2 names "Answers differ from submitted" (claim ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-025); the ruling uses the two wordings for one flag.

claims.statement: "Identification details" on the review page is marked up with a real GOV.UK heading class, not bold body text.
claims.quote: "Identification details" on the review gets a real GOV.UK heading class, not bold body text

claims.statement: That "Identification details" heading sits in a sensible hierarchy under the species heading.
claims.quote: in a sensible hierarchy under the species heading

claims.statement: Review cards get their accessible names the way the rest of the service does.
claims.quote: Review cards get their accessible names the way the rest of the service does.

claims.statement: A missing notification on the review page shows the standard page not found, like every other page in the service.
claims.quote: A missing notification on the review page shows the standard page not found, like every other page.

claims.statement: The plants notification lifecycle spec gets the missing blank line before its first scenario.
claims.quote: The plants notification lifecycle spec gets the missing blank line before its first scenario.

claims.statement: Delete on the notification view header opens the delete confirmation page, as a link rather than a post.
claims.quote: Delete on the header opens the delete confirmation page (a link, not a post).

claims.statement: Applying the one-form-each rule, Delete stays a link placed outside the Amend form and the Copy as new form.
claims.quote: Applying claim 2, it stays a link outside the Amend and Copy as new forms
claims.note: The bullet says "claim 2", which is the ruling's own numbered item 2 (claims ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-006 to ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-008), not a claim id in this extract.

claims.statement: No action on the notification view header shares another action's form.
claims.quote: so no action shares another's form

claims.statement: The ruling does not say which increments the fixes are grouped into, nor which fixes travel together, so "as few increments as sensible" leaves the grouping open.

The ruling does not list the atypical items item 4 sweeps up, so which fixes "every other atypical item the review found" covers is open on this source alone and has to come from the engineering review.
claims.note: Open point against claim ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-013. The review (review:engineering-2026-11-19) is a separate source.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what the future outstanding-actions banner is, when it arrives or what it shows, so the trigger for re-adding the stored outstanding items list and its rule is undefined.

The ruling does not name the "Answers differ from submitted" flag's field, its value for notifications that have never been submitted, or whether it is published on the notification event, so how the non-null flag is held and exposed is open.
claims.note: Open point against claims ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-025 and ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-026.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say at which heading level, or in what position on the page, the plants notification task list heading is shown, beyond that it is visible as in live animals.
claims.note: Open point against claims ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-002 and ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-003.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say which GOV.UK heading level "a sensible hierarchy under the species heading" means for "Identification details", nor what the species heading's own level is.
The ruling does not say what the callers of the two shared test helpers do once the overloads come out, nor how many call sites there are, so the replacement for each overloaded call is open.
